articleTitle: On the elimination of backscattering from straight wire systems
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Elimination of backscattering from a loaded straight wire scatterer and a multiply loaded parallel wire system scatterer has been considered. The problem is formulated in terms of surface integral equation based on the reaction concept. The unknown is the surface current which can be calculated using the method of moments. Appropriate loads have been determined yielding zero backscattering at a specified frequency for a plane wave incident on the wire system at any direction. A “frequency bandwidth for echo reduction” (FBER) has thus been defined for satisfactory operation of the loaded wire system. It has been found that if the center frequency is such that the wire is half-wave long, large FBER is obtained, reaching 55% of center frequency for 30 db reduction of backscattering keeping the loading determined at center frequency for zero backscattering unchanged.

articleTitle: Linear-sum mode arrays and beam forming
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In conventional phased arrays, antenna elements are usually simple radiators, such as dipoles, slots, dominant mode horns and microstrip patches, etc., that generate broadbeam, low gain and radiation patterns with a desired polarization property. The array beam is then formed and scanned by introducing phase shifts between the elements and modifying the phase shift values. The simplicity of array elements facilitates the design and then the fabrication. Also, because the element patterns are broad and often symmetric, with respect to the array axis, the beam scanning and its associated algorithm are easy to implement. In addition, this method of array design and beam scanning is general and can be used with different array configurations and electrical performance. However, a number of difficulties are often faced in such array implementations. Since each element, or each sub-array, needs a separate phase shifter, the array complexity and cost increases with its size and gain requirements. Also, the mutual coupling and array element pattern role off decrease the array gain for excessive scan. Furthermore, assuming array design can be achieved and implemented satisfactorily, the phase shifter insertion loss introduces an additional difficulty. Normally, this insertion loss limits the array performance in G/T, i.e. the gain to noise temperature ratio, for receive systems and the power efficiency for transmit systems. With microstrip arrays this phase shifter loss is accompanied by the feed line loss to further deteriorate the array performance.

articleTitle: EHF aperture-coupled microstrip antenna development
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Aperture-coupled microstrip antennas have been developed for operation in the millimeter wave region. A combination of patch dimensions and aperture size determines the antenna's resonating frequency. The measured return loss indicated an achievable bandwidth of 1.2% for a VSWR of less than 2:1. The measured radiation patterns at 45 GHz display the expected characteristics of microstrip patch antennas. Measurement of several antennas confirms the repeatability of the results.

articleTitle: A comparison study on wire-grid model and point matching technique with subdomain basis functions
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, the wire grid modeling technique is compared with subdomain basis functions using a point matching technique. The comparison for two dimensional case is carried out in the paper and that for three dimensional case will be given during the presentation. It is found that the wire grid modeling technique is an approximate model for the point matching technique with subdomain basis functions. The validation of the wire grid model is demonstrated and some questions arising in the application of the wire grid model are addressed.

articleTitle: Recent developments in the analysis and design of microstrip arrays
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Microstrip antenna array design is a rich and fascinating subject that has attracted the interest of antenna practitioners and analysts alike. This is partly due to the fact that microstrip arrays have a number of practical advantages, such as low cost, light weight, and conformability, that make them preferred over other antenna types for a variety of applications. But another reason for the interest in this subject is the fact that printed antennas offer more flexibility and variety in their design than probably any other class of antenna. The large number of possible permutations of element types, feeding methods, and substrate configurations has led to a wealth of novel and useful designs, and this trend shows no sign of diminishing [1]. This wide variety of microstrip array configurations also provides a fertile supply of challenging problems in analysis and modelling.

articleTitle: Application of the FEM to the analysis of the electromagnetic scattering from complex periodic structures
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A hybrid technique which combines the potentiality of the FEM in treating complex electromagnetic regions with the simplicity of the Floquet series has been presented. This results in a very powerful and flexible method for the analysis of periodic structures having arbitrary geometry and material properties.

articleTitle: Slot antennas on GaAs for integrated array applications
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Slot antennas are proposed for integration into GaAs monolithic phased arrays. The characteristics of suitable slot radiators are discussed and a technique for measuring the input impedance is described. Examples in the 20 to 30 GHz range show that the geometry of the slot may be varied to obtain input impedances which allow matching to either active MMIC devices or to a 50 Ω system.

articleTitle: Parametric analysis of an EMC patch surrounded by parasitic elements
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this study a single central patch with two or four peripheral parasitic patches was studied. They were identified as the 3CP and SCP antennas. It was found that the 3CP antenna has a wide impedance bandwidth, within which its radiation pattern remained practically constant. Its cross polar radiation was very low. Also, its size could be made small by compacting the configuration. This investigation shows that splitting a patch into three dipoles like narrow patches results in an antenna with a far more attractive performances. It also showed that adding two more dipoles to form the SCP antenna did not improve its performance and resulted in an inferior antenna.

articleTitle: Convergence criteria for TLM-PPM method application in printed antennas simulation
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: With this convergence criteria, the PPM can be easily used for the numerical processing of the TLM results. The time computation of this method has been reduced and this has allowed us the characterization of micros trip antennas. The use of a parallel computer should accelerate this process [4]. We think that this exploitation of the TLM results can be extended to other microwave structures and also perhaps to other numerical methods.

articleTitle: Modelling and simulation of crossing striplines in printed circuit boards or multichip modules
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The modelling and simulation of crossing striplines in printed circuit boards (PCBs) or multichip modules (MCMs) are presented in this paper by employing the boundary element method (13EM) to compute the per unit length capacitance, inductance, and resistance matrices. These parameters are then used to compute the cross-talk on the passive striplines generated by propagating waves on the driven striplines by the superposition of even and odd-mode components on the passive striplines. The physical load and line simulator (Phyllis) is used to simulate and analyze the signal propagations and cross-talk behaviors.

articleTitle: A new approach of pattern synthesis for array antennas of arbitrary geometry using the Conjugate Gradient method
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper we have presented a new approach for pattern synthesis for array antennas of arbitrary geometry. The far-field radiation pattern is matched to one that is prescibed by minimizing a global root-mean-square error. Using the Conjugate Gradient iterative scheme the storage and inversion of a large system matrix is omitted. As shown by numerical test cases presented in this paper, the present method offers an efficient and reliable numerical tool for (power) pattern synthesizing of arbitrary beam shapes.

articleTitle: Impedance properties of slots in NRD waveguide using the variational method
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A method of analysis for calculating the impedance of slots cut on the metal wall of a non radiative dielectric (NRD) waveguide is presented. With the aid of Parseval's theorem, an expression for the admittance, presented by the radiating slot to the feed NRD waveguide, is determined from the angular spectrum of plane waves and the discontinuity in modal current. In this analysis only the dominant LSM01 mode is assumed to be propagating. Numerical values agreed with previously reported experimental results.

articleTitle: On the use of the finite element method for RCS computation
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The finite element method (FEM) is well-suited for solving RF radiation and scattering problems for objects with complex structures and material properties including those having sharp edges, curved surfaces, and high aspect ratios because it uses fully unstructured mesh. These objects may have perfect conductors, lossy dielectric or magnetic materials, and multi-layered coatings. However, there are some major problems which must be resolved to successfully use such powerful method.

articleTitle: The radiation characteristics of an HF log-periodic antenna used for ground wave propagation
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Northern Radar's Cape Race prototype Ground Wave Radar (GWR) system employs a Log-periodic Dipole Array (LPDA) as the transmitter antenna. The LPDA is chosen due to its broadband, wide azimuthal beam width and high front to back ratio. The suitability of commercially available HF broadcasting LPDA antennas for use in GWR is investigated.

articleTitle: Extrapolating time domain data using autoregressive and Maximum Entropy Methods
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In recent years, considerable attentions have ban paid to time domain methods. The major part of these efforts have concentrated on applying Yee's (FD-TD), John's (TLM) or Begeron's algorithm to different structures. Nevertheless, the signal processing techniques for converting the resulting time domain data to frequency domain have been restricted to the DFT, FFT and Prony's methods. In this article two other extrapolation schemes are being presented which can be more suitable for applications involving resonant structures. The underlying theory accompanied by numerical simulations and relevant comparisons are presented.

articleTitle: A new formula for the line source field diffraction by a wedge
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A uniform solution is obtained for the diffraction of a cylindrical wave by a conducting wedge. This solution is valid within the entire region and the expression of the diffraction integral is obtained by Pauli-Clemmow method. When the source is far from the observation point and from the wedge, this solution reduces to that for the case of a plane wave illumination.

articleTitle: A waveguide/aperture-coupling technique for microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, we present a rectangular waveguide (RWG)/aperture technique intended to couple energy from active devices integrated on a GaAs substrate to patch antennas printed on a low permittivity substrate. By spacing the two substrates apart from each other, it is possible to remove heat from the structure through the metallic waveguide housing. This new approach also promises to reduce the number of power dividers required for phased array antennas.

articleTitle: Study of HF antenna coupling modes on the EC-130 aircraft
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The couplings between the HF antennas on the EC-130 aircraft are studied using computer modelling. A complex wire-grid model of the aircraft is used in conjunction with the Numerical Electromagnetic Code (NEC) to compute the currents on the antennas and on the aircraft and the radiation patterns when one of the antennas is excited by a voltage source. NEC runs are executed as frequency sweeps with fine frequency steps so that the detailed variations in inter-antenna couplings and radiation characteristics can be revealed. The numerical results provide a valuable and complete information set which is difficult to obtain by experimental measurements.

articleTitle: Analysis of the power handling capability of a superconducting stripline structure using complex images
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Power handling capability of a HTS strip depends on the maximum current density at its corners. In this paper, an efficient and numerically stable method was discussed to compute the current distribution over the cross section of a superconducting strip in a stripline structure. The problem is formulated in terms of a set of coupled integral equations for the interior and exterior regions. The method of moments was then used to solve the equations. An accurate fast convergent Green's function was used in the method for the exterior region. The exterior integral equation was also used to extend the output data of the moment method to approximate the current density very close to the comer.

articleTitle: A novel modal analysis formulation for multiple waveguide discontinuities
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: General multiple waveguide discontinuities are analyzed using modal analysis. The corresponding fields are expanded in modal form and the boundary conditions are imposed at each junction. Analytic expressions for the global scattering matrices are derived using a recurrence procedure that requires substantially less computation than the commonly used cascading techniques. The convergence and accuracy of the analytic expressions are illustrated for step-discontinuities in circular waveguides. Numerical results are presented for a thick iris in a circular waveguide.

articleTitle: Resonant frequency of dielectric ring resonator antenna
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A dielectric resonator (DR) placed in an open environment radiates strongly at and around its resonant frequencies. Among the advantages of DR antennas are their small size and no conductor loss. The other features of DR antennas are that each mode has a unique radiation pattern and the frequency bandwidth over which the antenna radiates efficiently can be controlled by choosing an appropriate value of the dielectric constant of the DR or by choosing an appropriate DR geometry. A dielectric ring resonator antenna has a greater operating frequency bandwidth than a cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna. In this paper, we compute the resonant frequency of a dielectric ring resonator antenna. It is shown that the simple perturbational technique is sufficiently accurate for computing the resonant frequency of a ring resonator antenna.

articleTitle: Dispersion characteristics of open microstrip using a direct VSW measurement approach
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An alternative experimental method for dispersion measurements in open microstrip is presented. The methods utilizes a scanning near field probe to directly measure the standing wave on the line under test. The guided wavelength is obtained by measuring the distance between successive voltage minimums . A variety of closed form dispersion expressions are included for comparison with experimental results. Previously investigated methods such as the sliding load and ring resonator technique s are also tested.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave scattering by two dielectric spheres with concentric dielectric layers
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The scattering by a single dielectric sphere with a concentric spherical shell has been analyzed in detail by a number of authors. It was firstly treated by Aden and Kerker [1] by expanding the exterior and interior fields in terms of the spherical vector wave functions. Later, Scharfman [2] used this solution to present numerical results for the special case of a small dielectric-coated conducting sphere. A solution for a conducting sphere coated with two concentric dielectric layers was given by Plonus [3]. Analytic solutions of the scattering by two or more spheres are given by the authors elsewhere [4,5].

articleTitle: S-parameter description of microstrip slot-couplers
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A method for the analysis of slot-coupled microstrip lines is presented. Expressions derived for the equivalent circuit impedances in terms of modal field expansions permit 5-parameters to be computed directly. Moreover, the derived 5-parameter expressions show a stationary nature with respect to the induced slot field. Preliminary measurements are in good agreement with theoretical predictions from 0.5 GHz to 18.0 GHz. Efficient computation and results which can be incorporated with existing CAD programs are advantages offered by this technique.

articleTitle: Pattern reconfiguration with an active integrated antenna
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An active integrated antenna element has previously been developed and presented [1]. The general configuration of this antenna is given in Fig. 1a) while the fabricated prototype antenna is given in Fig. 1b). This antenna utilizes active devices as part of the radiating structure, thus allowing both current amplitude and phase to be controlled along the antenna structure. This provides a control mechanism for antenna performance which is not possible with passive antennas. A unique feature of this antenna in its present topology is that the radiated pattern may be reconfigured with the integrated active devices. This may be achieved by altering the current phase distribution along the antenna structure. The fabricated antenna has been demonstrated to operate in its first order broadside mode and a higher order mode where conical shaped patterns are generated.

articleTitle: A dual orthogonal polarized microstrip antenna for use in the 20/30 GHz bands
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The use of microstrip arrays in the future generation of personal SATCOM terminals in the 2 0/30 GHz bands is highly attractive because of the cost and repeatability advantages of utilizing a printed architecture. Active elements can also be easily combined with a printed architecture to allow for tracking purposes. In addition, the low profile of printed arrays makes them ideal for hand-held terminals. This paper presents the design procedure and measured results for a novel 30 cm × 30 cm dual orthogonal polarized microstrip antenna in which the transmit and receive arrays share the same aperture, thus providing a size reduction advantage. Both orthogonally polarized arrays employ open-circuit stub radiators in a series configuration and are fed by two separate stripline corporate feeds.

articleTitle: Analysis of the coupling of vertical and horizontal dipoles in layered media
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The electromagnetic radiation and scattering by perfectly conducting objects of arbitrary shape involving both vertical and horizontal electric dipoles (VED and HED) in layered dielectric media has become an increasingly important topic of research and development. This is due to the several applications where the couplings of these dipoles are encountered. These applications include feeding probes and shorting posts in microstrip circuits, vias in microwave and digital integrated circuits, as well as vertical and inclined antennas near earth or ocean surface. This paper provides a technique to efficiently model the coupling of VED and HED in layered media. It starts by Sommerfeld choice of the vector potentials associated with the VED and HED in layered media. The scalar potentials are derived via the Lorentz gauge and are found to be different for charges associated with the VED and HED. The full wave spatial Green's functions are obtained using the complex image technique. This technique avoids the time-consuming Sommerfeld integrals and yield a highly convergent closed-form solution for the spatial Green's function. The solution has the form of superposition of real images which represent the low frequency solution, surface waves which are dominant in the far field, as well as complex images which include the radiation effect. The closed-form representation of the potential Green's functions enables one to efficiently use the moment method to model several practical structures involving both the VED and HED.

articleTitle: Computation of static capacitances for discontinuities in grounded coplanar waveguide by moment method
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The method of moment has been used for solving many electromagnetic problems, including computation of microstrip discontinuities[1]. In this paper, as far as we know, for the first time, this method is used to calculate the lumped element capacitances of some discontinuities in grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW). Discontinuities considered here are: 1) open-end and 2) gap in center conductor of GCPW. The effects of the substrate thickness, dielectric constant and the physical dimensions arc investigated.

articleTitle: Point-matching technique for EFIE with symmetrized impedance matrix
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The electric field integral equation for electromagnetic scattering by perfectly conducting cylinders is solved by the method of moments with weighted point matching technique. The associated impedance matrix is made symmetric by introducing a supplementary weighting factor and the resultant system of linear equations is solved by the Cholesky decomposition. This procedure yields a significant reduction in the necessary computer time and memory.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic modelling of a warship at high frequency
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper describes research work performed in the pursuit of a Masters of Engineering Degree at the Royal Military College of Canada, Kingston, Ontario. Here a Canadian warship is electromagnetically modelled using the generic “Wire-Grid Modelling” technique. This technique models the electrical characteristics of the exterior of the ship as a grid of interconnected perfectly conducting thin wires. The HF antennas on the ship are likewise modelled as thin wires and excited by voltages at their feed region. The resulting currents on the segment elements of the model and the fields surrounding the warship are computed using the NEC(3) computer program. The computed radiation patterns and antenna input impedance are compared to measurements made on a 1/50th scale-model. Since the segment mesh of the model serves only to approximate the electrical characteristics of the warship, the challenge in designing the model is to place the segments in locations where they will best represent the currents which would result on the surface of the ship from a similar excilation. Earlier work performed at Concordia University dealing with aircraft modelling has shown that with care, wire-grid modelling can produce accurate antenna impedance and radiation pattern results. The work presented here is a logical extension of this earlier aircraft work. Although the antenna types modelled here included whip, twin whip, and fan antennas, this paper will focus on the whip antenna.

articleTitle: Simple magnetic field model for complex three-dimensional power transmission line configurations
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A new computer program (MAGPLAN) is presented for the calculation of the magnetic flux density in the vicinity of complex three-dimensional power transmission corridors. This model represents an advance over existing software in the areas of enhanced useability and computation time. User input is minimized through a simple single-line plan view representation of the transmission corridor. Calculation time is reduced through Gauss-Legendre integration which is shown to be faster and likely more accurate than conventional straight line segmentation. Program results are in good agreement with fields measured within a complex Manitoba Hydro transmission corridor.

articleTitle: Estimation of ocean surface parameters by high frequency radar
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Over the last two decades, significant advances have been made in the use of high frequency (HF) Doppler radars for the remote sensing of various surface parameters in an ocean environment. Both narrow and broad beam arrays, operating in the ground wave mode at frequencies between 3 and 30 MHz, have been successfully employed in the determination of ocean currents, directional and nondirectional wave parameters , and surface winds.

articleTitle: RCS of dielectric cubes and rods by FDTD and by measurement
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper compares the RCS of plexiglas cubes and rods computed by the finite-difference time-domain(FDTD) method with the measured RCS. The measurement was done from 8 to 18 GHz, where the relative permittivity is approximately 2.3. Plexiglas is a relatively low-loss material and was approximated as lossless in the FDTD calculation. For each target the RCS was calculated with several values of ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> and FDTD's RCS was found to be very sensitive to ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>. FDTD traces out an intricate structure of peaks and sharp nulls. The calculated RCS shows good overall agreement with the measurement.

articleTitle: A pretreatment technique for the analysis of multi-object scattering problems
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: By dividing the contribution of the induced electric current density on each object into two parts, an efficient and simple numerical method is presented to solve the multi-object scattering problems. The formulation is provided for a two-dimensional scattering problem of perfectly-conducting cylinders and representative numerical results are given to show the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Calibration of an array antenna in the presence of multipath interference
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Presented is a method to estimate the element gains and phases of an array antenna when specular multipath interference is strong and cannot be ignored. A movable calibration source is used. The element gains are derived from the relative output powers at the array elements. The element phases are obtained by transforming the array snapshots to make the source direction appear fixed and then maximizing a function constructed with the transformed snapshots. Computer simulations produce highly accurate estimates of element gains and phases when the signal directions are known and the signal-to-noise ratio is reasonably high. When the directions are not known, the set of element phase estimates contains an additional component which produces a bias in direction estimates.

articleTitle: Precise design of multilayer circuit using finite differences techniques
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The design of multilayer directional couplers with septum is often done using the spectral domain technique. This technique consists in taking the Fourier transform of the boundary conditions and then expressing the charge distribution on the conductor, ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> and the septum, ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> as a function of G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ij</inf>, the Green function . Galerkin optimization technique is then used to compute ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> and ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> as a summation of arbitrary chosen basis functions, e.g., equation A proper choice of basis functions determines the precision and convergence of results.

articleTitle: A study on the scattering from a loaded spherical shell with an aperture
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, numerical results for the scattering of a plane wave by an infinitely-thin multiloaded perfectly-conducting spherical shell with a circular aperture are studied in order to get an insight of the scattering characteristics of the considered structure. It is found that filling the spherical shell with a dielectric doesn't change its scattering characteristics compared to those of the spherical shell presented alone or the closed spherical cavity. However, the existence of the dielectric inside the spherical shell alters the electrical size of the spherical shell which reduces the backscattering cross section but is still frequency sensitive. When the dielectric medium is presented as a coating layer, the scattering characteristics of the spherical shell are affected and the backscattering cross section is in general high far this type of loading.

articleTitle: Scattering properties of Archimedean spirals
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The use of spiral antennas is well known for EM radiation and reception but not so common for EM scattering. EM scattering differs from reception in that the response of the spiral is not limited to being observed from a pair of terminals but rather can be observed from any point surrounding the spiral. One consequence of this increased complexity is that although a spiral can be made to radiate and receive a single circular polarization, it does not follow that the radar cross-section of the spiral is significant only for an impinging wave with that given circular polarization.

articleTitle: Development of range test methodology for MLS antennas
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The importance of the Range Antenna geometry when testing MLS antennas is presented. The development of Coordinate Transformation Equations serves as a major tool in preparing test documentation or procedures. It also helps to quickly identify any problems due to the setup. Elevation antenna can be tested in its natural vertical position.

articleTitle: Microstrip fed annular slots in single and stacked configurations - studies of the effects of slot ground plane and back reflective plane on bandwidth and radiation characteristics
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The impedance and the radiation characteristics of single and stacked annular slots configurations were studied with emphasis on their dependence on various parameters such as: the slot width, the patch-to-slot spacing (for stacked configurations only), the form of the slot ground plane (SGP) and the presence of a back reflective plane (BRP). It was found that the impedance bandwidth is mainly controlled by the geometry of the radiating element (i.e., the slot width and the slot-to-patch spacing, where applicable) being only slightly dependent on the form of the SGP. The input impedance levels are also controlled by the same parameters but may change drastically with the form of the SGP, especially for slots in single configurations with a BRP. The radiation characteristics, however, are mainly controlled by the geometry of the SGP and the presence of a BRP. Whenever a particular application asks for a SGP larger then the wavelength the use of a SGP form able to reduce the effects of the edge diffraction is imperious and may enhance the performance capability of the radiators. Finally, the advantages of stacked configurations were presented. It can be concluded that the annular slot in a stacked configuration with a circular microstrip patch on top is a versatile element with wide impedance and gain bandwidths. All that, together with the very low level of feedline spurious radiation make this element most suitable for high performance array applications [2].

articleTitle: FD-TD analysis of waveguide components using dispersive boundary conditions (DBC)
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The dispersive absorbing boundary condition (DBC) developed in [1] for microstrip component analysis, a case where dispersion is week, is now applied to a strongly dispersive case which occurs in conductor waveguides. The absorbing quality of the DBC is found to be much superior to that of the absorbing boundary conditions that are currently used for waveguide component analysis. Due to the significant performance improvement and the easy implementation of the DBC, the accuracy and the efficiency can be improved greatly when applying the boundary condition to waveguide component analysis.

articleTitle: Computer modeling of MLS signal strength in the presence of runway hump shadowing
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A complete, automated approach for predicting absolute MLS signal strength for sites involving irregular terrain profiles is presented. The approach involves two computer models: one to convert raw terrain elevation data into a linear profile, and the other to estimate path loss using the Geometrical Theory of Diffraction. Because the entire process is automated, little expertise on the part of the user is required. Validation of the approach is given by comparisons of measured and modeled signal strength data for a representative MLS site.

articleTitle: A field-theory-based technique for the group-delay analysis of rectangular waveguide filters
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Group delay analysis of rectangular waveguide filters using a rigorous field-theory-based technique is presented . In order to provide an accurate approach for the transmission phase calculation and its derivative with respect to frequency, the procedure includes higher-order mode excitation and interaction effects at all discontinuities involved. The predicted group delay and magnitude responses are compared to measurements on evanescent-mode T-septum bandpass and millimeter-wave E-plane filter prototypes. Results are shown to be in good agreement.

articleTitle: Improved characteristics of microstrip disc antenna using passive circular array
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Mutual Coupling between radiating elements in a microstrip array antenna has aroused attention in recent years. Numerous papers and research reports have been published that deal with their effects on the antenna performances. It is known that in an active array the coupling may cause increased sidelobe levels, reduced gain, main beam squint, mismatch between the antenna and feed system, etc. Ample efforts have been put on the prediction and cancellation of these harmful effects on the fully active array. However, the electromagnetic energy can transfer between either active and passive elements since the mutual coupling is only structural dependent. By placing some passive elements closely adjacent to the active elements, all elements of the system can be excited and radiate energy. The characteristics of the mixed system can be altered by changing the distance between the elements. One of the simplest mixed structures is a hexagonal seven element array with only the central element fed, as shown in Fig. 1. Each element of the circular passive array will be excited by the central microstrip disc due to the mutual coupling. By carefully choosing the distance between the elements, to some degree, desired and improved characteristics may be obtained.

articleTitle: Invisible u-shaped slot communications antenna
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The increase of vandalism and pilferage of vehicle installed communication equipment and antennas has created a need for invisible radio antennas in the UHF band. Users of cellular telephone and law-enforcement under-cover teams desire to disguise their radio and antenna equipment to prevent theft, breakage, and exposure. This paper presents an inexpensive invisible, i.e. covert, antenna design for two-way communication, for both vehicle mounted and below-ground installations.

articleTitle: Limited scan antenna for low-cost experimental array radar
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The performances of a narrow band lens with 12% bandwidth (11.50 to 13.0 GHz) and a wide band lens with 36% bandwidth have been evaluated. The balun for the narrow band design was synthesized to give a VSWR of 1.2 while that of the wide band lens gave a VSWR of 1.90. The delay line is assumed to be in stripline with a loss of 0.10 db/ins and a substrate dielectric constant of 2.3. A rectangular grid of 24 × 24 elements spaced 0.654 ins. apart is used to sample the focal region field. This feed array is excited by a smaller grid of 16 × 16 subarray ports. A Taylor distribution of - 45 dB sidelobe is imposed across the aperture. The resulting focal region distribution for azimuth beam scan of −5.5° is plotted in Fig. 4 and the transformed distribution at the subarray ports is depicted in Fig. 5, both computed at 11.5 GHz. Each grid line in the plots represents a row or column of elements or ports. This particular feed array can only achieve secondary beam scan of ±5°. At 5.5° of scan, the array has failed to capture some of the higher energy field lines. A larger array must, be used for wider scan. As expected, the amplitude distribution, normalised to the total input power, of the subarray ports remains more or less symmetric, eventhough the beam is scanned, and mostly unchanged with frequency. Only the phase distribution of the subarray ports needs to be adjusted. similar plots are made for the difference pattern. Examination of the sum and difference mode plots shows that the corner subarray ports are not needed because of their low level of excitation.

articleTitle: Time domain Finite Element solution of electromagnetic field problems
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The application of the Finite Element method to the solution of three-dimensional time dependent electromagnetic field problems is investigated. The mathematical formulation is based on an expanded form of the vector wave equation, with local absorbing boundary conditions. The formulation is discretized using finite elements in the spatial domain and finite differences

articleTitle: New Transmission-Line Matrix (TLM) models for the two-dimensional wave equation
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Three new Transmission-Line Matrix (TLM) models applicable to two-dimensional electromagnetic field problems are presented. The unique properties of the new TLM models are related to the approximation of spatial derivatives in their equivalent Finite Difference algorithms. The significance of this work is to demonstrate that some of the inherent flexibility of the Finite Difference and Finite Element methods (i.e., various grid structures and altering the order of accuracy) is also applicable to the TLM method. The benefits associated with the increased flexibility are improved modelling of geometrical features and increased accuracy.

articleTitle: Performance of biconical antennas at low frequencies
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Planar wire model biconical antennas with flare angle of 30°, 60°, and 90°, and various hat angles are examined using the method of moment. It is found that the planar model does not exhibit the same broadband performance as the body-of-revolution model. It is also found that increasing the hat angle, while holding the flare angle constant, has the effect of increasing the input impedance at the anti-resonant frequency. Adding a cross onto the planar wire biconical antenna with flare angle of 60° is also studied. It is observed that the broadband performance of the antenna improves with the modification. The antenna factor of the wire antennas are also computed to compare their performance.

articleTitle: An error model for automated swept-angle bistatic scattering measurements
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In recent years we have developed an automated swept-angle bistatic scattering measurement system (ASBSMS). The measurement system fixes the target and direction of illumination, then sweeps the receive antenna to collect data as a direct function of bistatic angle. A practical procedure is presented for estimating the measurement errors, which can be large because of the high coupling between the transmit and receive antennas near forward scatter. The procedure uses data collected at the time of measurement and can be applied in the laboratory to reveal problems in the system. In addition, a simple spatial filtering scheme is given that can be used to reduce the measurement error. Comparisons of measurements with the numerical solution to the dual-surface magnetic field integral equation for scattering from conducting cones and cubes demonstrate the error model and filtering scheme.

articleTitle: SAR distributions of a four element interstitial hyperthermia array
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Hyperthennia induced by interstitial microwave applicators has proven to be effective in the treatment of malignant tumors particularly when used in conjunction with ionizing radiation and chemotherapeutic drugs. During hyperthermia treatment the tumor temperature is raised above 42°C at which point many normal cellular functions are impaired. Cancer cells have been shown to be more sensitive to elevated temperature than normal cells, however temperature extremes can cause damage and even burning of healthy tissue. It is thus of primary importance to ensure that the power density is sufficiently high to reach therapeutic temperatures in the entire tumor and decays rapidly outside the tumor volume.

articleTitle: MLS azimuth antenna ground crossfall considerations
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: It has been recognized that the ground reflection for the AZ MLS antenna can cause significant error. After many years of development the vertical aperture size of the AZ antenna is now generally specified such that it is sufficiently large to satisfy an 8 dB/° slope requirement at 0° elevation angle. This requirement is satisfied with a 1.2 m (4 ft) vertical aperture size. During the early phases of the MLS development it was demonstrated that a 1.2 m vertical aperture size would provide adequate suppression of the ground reflection. (The Hazeltine Corporation implemented, in 1973, a Doppler MLS planar beam AZ array antenna with a 1.2 m vertical waveguide-column radiators.) A quantitative relationship between a performance parameter and the vertical aperture size is not readily available. It is believed that the error caused by the ground crossfall (lateral tilt of the ground) at the reflection point is the controlling factor which determines the size of the vertical aperture. A simple relationship has been derived which relate guidance angle error, crossfall angle and vertical aperture size.

articleTitle: A novel class of slotline printed antennas over ferrite substrates
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The Magvi, Aerial, a printed vivaldi type slotline element, printed in a ferrite substrate, is introduced. The design of the shape of the edges for the slotline taper will be discussed. The practical results presented by a prototype will be shown and commented. Finally, some conclusions and suggestions for future works will be given.

articleTitle: Exact solution to electromagnetic scattering by a spheroidal boss on a plane surface
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An exact solution to the problem of scattering of a plane wave by a hemispheroidal boss on an infinite perfectly conducting plane, has been obtained using a similar solution for scattering by a single spheroid in an unbounded space. Numerical results have been presented for perfectly conducting bosses of different sizes, and axial ratios. On the basis of this exact solution, the analysis of electromagnetic scattering by rough surfaces modeled as various configurations of hemispheres on planar surfaces can be extended to the more general and more practical case of spheroidal bosses of arbitrary axial ratios.

articleTitle: Remote sensing water content in a clay / sand mixture using Impedance Computed Tomography
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The Impedance Computed Tomography method provides a way to measure groundwater infiltration of bentonite clay / sand mixture being considered as a buffer in a nuclear fuel waste disposal vault. It is a remote sensing technique using current stimulation. An iterative algorithm called the “Algorithm of Wexler” is used to process the voltage measurements. The algorithm models the buffer material as a distribution of admittances. Important to this application is to understand the electrical properties of the buffer material. In situ measurements of the resistivity and capacitance of reference buffer were made and the results are discussed in the context of the design of a data logging system for field tests using this method.

articleTitle: Measured scattering patterns of geometric shapes in the resonant frequency range
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Precision RCS pattern measurements over a wide frequency range were carried out on targets consisting of simple geometric shapes such as cubes, rods with square and circular cross-section, disks, cone-spheres, square and triangular pyramids and bodies of revolution. The size of targets was chosen so that measurements would encompass the resonance size range (≈0.1–6λ). Perfectly conducting targets and dielectric targets were measured. Results of some of these measurements are presented along with details of the measurement system and procedure used. The data is presented in the form of contour maps on a polar grid. A study of these maps provides meaningful insight into scattering mechanisms. The data is also available in digital form and may be used as reference data for the validation of analysis techniques and computer codes and for developing modelling guidelines for the use of these codes.

articleTitle: The performance of conical reflectors with a microstrip comb line array feed
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The expression for the far field patterns of conical reflectors with a line source feed in the form of two microstrip comb line arrays, are derived and computed using a numerical integration of the physical optics currents. Representative radiation patterns are computed and presented.

articleTitle: Resonant radiation resistance in circular-spherical microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents the theoretical analysis on the resonant radiation resistance of spherical-circular microstrip antenna and discuss the effect of feed location on the value of radiation resistance. On the previous work in reference [1], a variety of the analytic results are obtained from the Green's function formulation in the spectral domain. These results are employed to further derive the radiated power. On the other hand, feed point voltage is analyzed by the cavity model. As result of this, the radiation resistance is determined analytically. Finally, the numerical result will be compared with the data obtained from GTLM method in order to validate our theory.

articleTitle: Simple mathematical model for the analysis of superconductor joints
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The model presented gives a simple and efficient evaluation of the physical behaviour of a conductor-superconductor joint. The value of the joint resistance obtained for our example is bigger than the optimum value for such joints, which is about 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−8</sup>Ω. This is mainly due to our solder thickness of 0.9mm, which is substantially bigger than the better values, down to 0.05mm as reported in [2].

articleTitle: Application of integral equations to RCS computations of complex material targets
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The equivalence principal is used to formulate the scattered field in terms of equivalent surface currents radiating in unbounded free space. The method of moment is then used to reduce the integral equations to a matrix equation. The method is applied to compute the radar cross-section of material targets.

articleTitle: Synthesis of rectangular microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Up to day there is no available synthesis method for rnicrostrip antenna design. Analytical expressions of impedance using cavity model have been previously developed. The aim of this communication is to derive expressions to synthesize the dimensions of patches for given resonant frequency, input resistance, and substrate.

articleTitle: Merging the Method of Lines with the Spectral Domain Method: The Space-Spectral Domain Approach (SSDA)
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A new hybrid numerical technique, the Space-Spectral Domain Approach (SSDA), has been developed to analyze planar circuit discontinuities. The method combines in one algorithm a space discretization method, the Method of Lines (MoL), with the Spectral Domain Approach (SDA), which is a Fourier domain technique. The SSDA was originally developed as full-wave analysis technique to calculate resonant frequencies of planar circuits and has recently been extended to include self-consistent hybrid boundary conditions to calculate also scattering parameters of arbitrarily shaped circuit discontinuities. A deterministic quasi-static SSDA has also been developed very recently to provide a quick first order design response. This paper focusses on the development of the quasi-static SSDA to introduce the basics for this algorithm. Theoretical data for conductor backed coplanar transmission lines will be presented and the accuracy of the method compared with measurements.

articleTitle: Radiation and scattering analysis of two-dimensional conducting and dielectric objects using the generalized multiple multipole technique
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, the generalized multiple multipole technique [1] is used to solve for the problems of scattering and radiation by cylinders of arbitrary cross section. The formulation is carried out for the problems of homogeneous dielectric, imperfectly and perfectly conducting cylinders. The problems are formulated using sets of fictitious multipole sources to simulate the fields of the cylinders. Application of the boundary conditions yields a system of linear equations which can be solved for the unknown expansion coefficients.

articleTitle: Comparison of super-resolution techniques in scattering analysis
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Recently, several spectral estimation techniques which offer significantly higher resolution than the conventional DFT technique have been introduced. The use of these techniques in scattering analysis is presented in this paper. The emphasis is placed on two methods; MUSIC method and adaptive auto-regressive method based on the LMS approach. A comparative performance evaluation of these two techniques is reported. The study is based on the time domain analysis of the frequency domain RCS return which is dispersive in nature.

articleTitle: A comparison of the planar and spherical approaches to near-field measurement's
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Table 1 presents a summarised comparison of the features of planar and spherical near-field measurement systems.

articleTitle: A single-arm spiral antenna
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An array consisting of four-by-four spiral antennas is constructed using the pair-element (PE) technique. The 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth is improved to 8.9% by the PE technique from 3.8% for an array without using the PE technique. The −14-dB return loss bandwidth is widened to 6.4% from 3.6%. In addition, a beam with a tilt angle of 21 degrees is demonstrated, where the spiral elements are excited in 90-degree phase steps.

articleTitle: A systematic treatment of conversion of vector wave functions
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The problem of radiation and wave propagation in two-medium or multimedium is a important aspect of engineering electromagnetism. The most interesting electromagnetic phenomena are induced by surfaces of discontinuity or rapid change in the physical properties of the medium . It is therefore the case that we often encounter electromagnetic problems whth multi-boundaries in applications of electromagnetic theory. For example, there are flat and spherical or cylindrical coordinate surfaces in the problems of scattering from spherical or cylindrical objects in two-medium half spaces. However, how to expand boundary conditions on two different boundary surfaces is a difficult problem. Fortunately, we can overcome this difficulty by using conversion technique of vector wave functions. In the following, we present a systematic treatment of the conversion technique and some applications. For ease of representation, the vector wave function expansions of electromagnetic field is discussed briefly, at first.

articleTitle: Full-wave analysis of finite large printed dipole arrays using the Conjugate Gradient - FFT method
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The full-wave analysis of finite large printed dipole arrays is performed by the Conjugate Gradient - FFT method with full wave discrete image technique. The CG-FFT method has the merits of saving computer memory (O(N)) and computing time (O(4N(l + log<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(N)))), compared with the conventional Moment Methods (O(N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) and O(N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>), respectively). This makes the CG-FFT method very suitable for efficient analysis of large electromagnetic structures. In this paper, combined with the full-wave discrete image technique, CG-FFT is applied to analyze the finite large printed antenna arrays. Several types of finite large printed dipole arrays are analyzed and the numerical results are discussed.

articleTitle: Low profile slotted Microstrip Antenna for cellular mobile radio
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode of a circular resonant microstrip cavity has been used to produce an omni-directional, vertically polarized antenna with a broadside null. Interlaced circumferential slots were added resulting in reductions in the resonant frequency of up to 50%. The performance of this antenna when mounted on the roof of an automobile has been analyzed through the application of the Geometric Theory of Diffraction (GTD).

articleTitle: Progress in TLM modeling of microwave structures
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: While the basic TLM modeling procedures for electromagnetic field analysis are well understood and applied by an increasing number of researchers and designers, further refinement in the description of boundaries, field partitioning, and acceleration of numerical procedures are being developed. This paper focusses on recent progress in these areas and demonstrates the resulting improvements in modeling capability, accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: High temperature superconducting small helical antenna
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A complete analysis for high-temperature superconducting small helical antenna has been investigated. Moment method technique is used to calculate the input impedance end radiation pattern of the helix. The helix is driven from a balanced twin-lead transmission line for maximum power transmission. The effect of different parameters of the helix, as pitch angle a and number of turns N on the radiation efficiency has been calculated.

articleTitle: Determination of rock and coal conductivities by using electromagnetic wave propagation
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Knowledge of the conductivity distribution in the surrounding media is essential for the study of the subsurface propagation of the electromagnetic waves. There are two main categories of methods currently used for measuring the conductivities. namely laboratory methods and methods using a direct electric contact. Due to the difficulties in maintaining the sample rocks exactly in the same conditions as in underground (moisture level, temperature, pressure, etc.), the conductivity values measured in the laboratory are not useful, being usually one or even two orders of magnitude lower than the real values. Although the methods using the electric contact make it possible to measure the rock conductivities directly in the underground, perfect galvanic contact on the rock surface is difficult to achieve due to the electrode polarization, high transition resistances, local inhomogeneities and stray fields from cables, which affect a great deal the precision of the measurements. In this paper we present another method, based on the wave propagation [1], which allows the determination of conductivities in a given region and removes the disadvantages of the previous methods.

articleTitle: Scattering by a perfectly conducting slotted elliptic cylinder
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The problem of scattering by a perfectly conducting slotted elliptic cylinder excited by a z polarized incident plane wave is considered. The problem is reduced to an integral equation in terms of the aperture field. The solution of the integral equation is carried out using two methods. In the first method, the aperture field is expressed analyticly, then Galerkin's technique is introduced to solve for the unknown aperture field coefficients. In the second method, method of moments is employed along with the point matching technique to solve for the unknown expansion coefficients.

articleTitle: Comparison of EM response in time and frequency domains
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper is concerned with the use of time- and frequency-domain codes for computing the interaction of electromagnetic waves with simple and complex structures. An example chosen for this study is a cubic box with the top open. The Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method is used for computing time-domain responses to an electromagnetic pulse (EMP), a Gaussian pulse, and a sine wave. Frequency-domain results are obtained by using a moment method solution of the electric field integral equation (EFIE). Comparison is then made, both in the frequency and time domains, on corresponding quantities using Fourier transforms. Effects of various factors - the shape of the incident waveform, discretization of the structure, and Fast Fourier Transformation - on the CPU time and the accuracy of the solution are demonstrated. Guidelines are established for obtaining an accurate response.

articleTitle: Accelerated 3D surveillance by beam broadening and multiple beams
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In phased array radars with multifunction capability different modes of operation - surveillance, acquisition and tracking - compete for the allocation of time and power. Especially in 3D surveillance planar arrays with pencil beams suffer from the large number of beam positions to be processed.

articleTitle: The realization of IDGH gain rhombic antenna in the UHF band using tapered U-shaped arms
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In the early days, the rhombic antenna gained favour because of its wide band frequency characteristics. This type of antennas was first introduced in the early 1930's [1], They were used primarily in the HF band. Until recently, travelling wave rhombic antennas have never been seriously considered for the use in the UHF band where they may have many advantages over the standing wave antennas [2]. A previous study [3,4] of the travelling wave V-antennas revealed that these antennas do not lend themselves to increase in the directional gain by increasing the length of the antenna arms indefinitely. This was attributed to the radiation of most of the power from the input end of the antenna leaving relatively low power to be radiated from the far ends. A similar study showed clearly that the end sections of the arms of tubical travelling wave rhombic antennas do not radiate appreciably and the directional gain of the antenna cannot be increased by increasing the arms of the antenna beyond a certain limit.

articleTitle: Radiated fields from transient signals on open microstrip
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Advances in semiconductor technology have seeded rapid growth and performance of high speed communications and signal processing electronics and their implementation in large systems. These systems require long interconnect lines, usually microstrip, supporting fast rise time signals and often terminated with non-linear devices. Due to the possibility of interference between between signal conductors on the same system and with other systems it is important to be able to evaluate and control the radiated transient fields generated by the interconnect structures. Furthermore, the spectral content of the radiated far field can be quite different than that of the signal line current waveform due to the radiation mechanism of the printed line source as well as the propagation/termination properties of the interconnect structure.

articleTitle: Finite-element analysis of T-septum waveguide structures
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The cutoff wavelength, the bandwidth and the plots of field of hollow and dielectric-loaded T-septum waveguide structures Crectangular T-septum waveguides with specific configurations, ridged and channel waveguides with a T-shaped find are computed by finite element method. The ways of improving the characteristics like increasing bandwidth, a minimization of sizes and so on, are analysed.

articleTitle: Scattering by a non-confocal dielectric coated homogeneous elliptic cylinder
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The scattering properties of a homogeneous elliptic cylinder with a nonconfocal dielectric coating are investigated analytically. The method of separation of variables together with the addition theorem for Mathieu functions are used to determine, exactly , the field distributions in each region for the transverse magnetic (TM) excitation. The technique can be easily extended to handle any number of layers.

articleTitle: Design considerations in achieving MLS category III continuity of service requirements
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper addresses system design aspects that should be considered in designing Microwave Landing Systems (MLS) to meet Category III Continuity of Service Requirements. Experience with Instrument Landing Systems (ILS) has shown that the continuity of service achieved in the field is at least two times worse than performance prediction based on equipment reliability. This is primarily due to outages caused by environmental factors. In the development of MLS it has been assumed that it would be more immune to environmental outages than ILS. This paper addresses these and other factors that should be considered in designing MLS to achieve Category III continuity of service requirements.

articleTitle: Results of MLS antenna range tests
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The results of Azimuth and Elevation Antenna range tests show that MLS-400T series provides very stable and accurate MLS guidance signals.

articleTitle: Analysis of the reflection properties of rectangular elements printed on a dielectric slab
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The spectral domain dyadic Green's function is developed for stratified media. Poisson summation formula is used to transform the infinite spectral integrals into infinite double summations for discrete frequencies and make it applicable to infinite arrays of conductors printed on a dielectric slab. A Galer kin method is used to descertize and solve the electric field integral equations for the geometry of a two dimensional array of rectangular patches.

articleTitle: Improvements and new applications of FDTD method
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this work new finite difference expressions for FDTD are derived to compute the magnetic field components in the vicinity of a doubly coated conducting plane sheet. The derivation of these expressions is based on the Faraday's law in integral form. Electric field magnitudes are computed in the presence of a doubly coated conducting plate using the newly derived expressions and compared with those of a finer FDTD mesh, good agreement between the two computations is observed.

articleTitle: Microwaveim aging of inhomogenious dielectric cylinders
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A method of reconstructing the dielectric cross-section of inhomogenious cylinders using microwaves is investigated. The method uses the information found in the scattered field produced from an illuminating plane wave to reconstruct the physical properties of the cylinders. The two-dimensional integral equation for the scattered field is transformed into a set of linear equations using the method of moments. The resulting matrix is ill-conditioned and is solved by a conjugate gradient method to give a least squares solution. The method is demonstrated by computer simulation, and some results are presented.

articleTitle: Combining electromagnetics and digital signal processing: Moving towards the intelligent antenna
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper we have described the evolution that is taking place in antenna engineering. Antennas are now being interfaced with active devices, thereby making them integrated antennas; and, as well, they are about to be interfaced to digital logic, which in turn will lead to intelligent antennas. The art of antenna engineering being expanded by the requirement for algorithmic development, digital logic design, software development, modelling of passive and active components and the need for antenna architects to make sure that all these pieces fit together. We are now experiencing the movement towards the integration of electromagnetics and digital signal processing.

articleTitle: Nonuniformity in a class of UTD curved surface fields near smooth, convex surfaces
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Two different creeping wave formulations are examined in this paper. One is valid for source and field points on or near the curved surface, the other is valid for source and field points off the curved surface. This paper uses a numerical experiment with a circular cylinder to determine at which height the two different formulations overlap.

articleTitle: Finite element application to electromagnetic interference problems
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper describes possible applications of finite element method to EMI/C problems. The applications are related to crosstalk problems on printed circuit boards, and calculation of losses on printed circuit board environment.

articleTitle: Diakoptic theory and the complex images for microwave integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents an approach for rapid computation of microwave integrated circuit. The scheme includes the integral equation, a rapidly convergent Green's function by complex images, a multi-pipe method for large segments, and the diakoptic moment method. The scheme reduces the solution time of a two-stager MMIC amplifier of 411 segments to 3 minutes per frequency on a 33MHZ 80386 personal computer.

articleTitle: Analysis of pulse propagation in ferrite filled waveguides
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Ferrites are anisotropic in their electromagnetic properties. In the frequency domain, these properties are described by an intrinsic permeability tensor. Members of this tensor are functions of the ferrite saturation magnetization, the magnetic field intensity, effective gyromagnetic ratio and the intrinsic linewidth. At microwaves, both real and imaginary parts of the Polder permeability tensor [1] are frequency dependent and form typical dispersive and resonant relations. At constant biasing conditions, values describing ferrite properties may be computed from measured quantities by using a combined experimental-theoretical method [2]. It is commonly believed that this method offers more accurate results of the permeability tensor than the method based on the theoretically predicted values. In particular, measurements of ferrite-loaded waveguides in the X-band (or I-band in the JCS standard) provide the frequency spectra of various loading configurations.

articleTitle: Power deposition properties of a travelling-wave applicator for interstitial hyperthermia
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A permittivity of (51-j31) has been used which is typical of muscle, skin and other tissue having high water content [2) at the frequencies considered here (915 MHz). The radiator has been modeled as a lossy transmission line with empirically determined characteristics. Figures 2 and 3 show the power density along a line parallel to the axis of the applicator at various radial distances with the diode biased on. The rapid rate of decay with radial distance could be reduced by operating at a lower frequency. Figure 4 illustrates the movement of the peak power density as the diodes are switched on or off. In Figure 5 the length of the applicator has been increased to one half wavelength. The two modes are shown to provide uniform heating over a 6 cm range of depth

articleTitle: Derivation of TLM type methods from characteristic field decompositions
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A series of general Transmission Line Matrix (TLM) type methods are derived directly from Maxwell's curl equations without recourse to transmission line models. Written as a system of conservation laws, Maxwell's equations are decomposed along the orthogonal characteristic directions of a rectangular grid. The Riemann Invariants in this method correspond to the Voltage Pulses of the TLM method. Details are given for the 2-D TMy case but this method is not restricted to two dimensions and has been derived for the general 3-D case.

articleTitle: Transient current distribution on a cylinder illuminated by a plane wave
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Transient scattering of an impulsive plane electromagnetic wave by a perfectly conducting circular cylinder has been studied extensively and results are available in the literature [1,2]. Expressions have been obtained for early and late times, which are represented by separate formulas. Since the early-time solution is only valid for a very short time period immediately after the arrival of the wavefront and the late-time solution is valid after the wavefront has completely passed the cylinder, the intermediate time interval is too large for some angular region to obtain accurate results via simple interpolations of the early- and late-time results. In this paper, we derive a single formula which is mathematically valid for all the time ranges and rapidly convergent for the time range after the instant the incident wavefront has passed the cylinder axis.

articleTitle: Analysis of guided-wave structure for millimeter-wave integrated circuits design
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this work, the inverted strip dielectric waveguide is studied using the mode matching and the method of effective dielectric constant. The fields are expanded in terms of two scalar potentials in different layers. Application of boundary conditions, namely the continuity of tangential fields result in system of linear homogeneous equations which are solved numerically. The field distributions and the propagation constants are then determined. The leakage due to the surface wave propagation in the guiding layer is also calculated.

articleTitle: The effect of shadowing by a runway hump on MLS signal strength
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The BDP method can be easily and accurately applied to model humped runways. Because of its “easy to use”, the method is a promising tool for the estimation of the power density and to examine the effect of shadowing by runway hump on MLS signal strength.

articleTitle: Space-qualified circularly-polarized subarray for satellite communications
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Design and experimental results of an L-Band circularly-polarized microstrip subarray are presented in this paper. A 2 × 2 subarray of vertically-stacked microstrip patches is fed by a microstrip beamforming network in a sequentially phase-rotated fashion. The subarray is composed of space-qualified materials and is intended as a feed element for reflectors on board communications satellites. Measured return loss and far-field pattern performance across the 30 MHz bandwidth are included.

articleTitle: DME/P antenna requirements analysis and modeling
publicationTitle: 1992 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The precision distance measuring equipment (DMF/P) antenna forms a part of the Microwave Landing System (MLS). The antenna and associated transponder, provide precision distance information to properly configured user aircraft. Antenna performance parameters required to meet system level power density requirements are presented. FAA and ICAO antenna requirements are compared. Antenna pattern synthesis using individual level control of each sidelobe and filled null is used Optimized free space and installed antenna patterns are described.

articleTitle: A new method for obtaining elevation angle with a fan-beam radar
